resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy Transfer (Resale Application / housing inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Pemberton Township Code Enforcement Division (Housing Code Official), Department of Community Development
resale_co.valid_for: The application expires 60 days after it is filed and cannot be transferred. How long the certificate itself is valid is not stated.
requirements: House number on the dwelling, reflective, at least 3.5 inches high and readable from the street
Fences and pool areas with self-latching, outward-swinging gates (fence at least 48 inches, latch at least 54 inches)
Landings and porches 30 inches or higher need a guard rail at least 36 inches high with openings no wider than 4 inches
Stairways, decks, porches and balconies structurally sound; handrail on any stair with 4 or more risers
No broken or missing glass; windows open, lock and have screens; egress windows open easily
Basement outside entrances kept tight against pests and water
Anti-tilt device on the stove; all utilities on at the time of inspection
Smoke alarm on every level, in every bedroom and outside each sleeping area (form says battery operated)
Carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage
ABC fire extinguisher, 5 to 10 lb, mounted in a visible, convenient spot (April 2026 form still lists it)
Bathroom window or exhaust fan vented outside
Mechanical equipment (exhaust fans, sump pumps, wood stoves, fireplaces) safe and working
No electrical hazards: no open junction boxes, taped splices or extension-cord wiring; service wire in sound condition
GFCI protection for pools, spas, exterior and garage outlets, within 5 feet of water, and at kitchen and bath counters
Certifications may be required for roof, electrical, structural or heating items

fees.label: Resale inspection (initial inspection)
fees.quote: A $150.00 fee must accompany the application for inspection. This fee covers the initial inspection.

fees.label: Each reinspection
fees.quote: For each subsequent reinspection, the application shall notify the Housing Code Official in writing and shall submit the reinspection fee of $50.00.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Resale Application (dated 04.29.26) from the Code Enforcement/Housing Forms page. Fill it out completely and submit it with the $150 fee to the Housing Code Official's office in the Municipal Building, 500 Pemberton-Browns Mills Road (the checklist says payment goes to the cashier's office). Inspectors in the field do not accept applications or fees, and nothing is scheduled until the application is complete and paid. If the buyer is taking responsibility for the certificate, notify the office in writing before it is issued.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Occupancy Transfer is required in the Township of Pemberton EACH time a residential dwelling unit changes occupant.
An application for inspection must be completely filled out and submitted to the Housing Code Official’s Office in the Township of Pemberton Municipal Building.
Applications are non-transferrable and will expire after 60 days.
All application and fees must be submitted to the Housing Code Officials Office. Applications and/or fees will not be accepted by the inspectors in the field.
Note: Re-inspection fee is $50. For any questions, email us at wjones@pemberton-twp.com and/or mknoblock@pemberton-twp.com.
Code Enforcement Department 500 Pemberton Browns Mills Rd Pemberton, NJ, 08015 Phone (609) 894-3376
Code Enforcement Division Michael Knoblock Wendy Jones

resale_co.notes: The township calls it a Certificate of Occupancy Transfer, required each time a dwelling changes occupant (sale or rental). Staff titles for Wendy Jones and Michael Knoblock are not published; the Code Enforcement page lists them under the Code Enforcement Division, and the form tells applicants to email either one (mknoblock@pemberton-twp.com is the second contact). The office secretary is Ashlee Bartole, 609-894-3376. The separate Rental Application (also dated 04.29.26) uses the same $150 fee but lists a $100 reinspection fee; the Resale Application says $50.

requirements: Smoke alarm on every level, in every bedroom and outside each sleeping area
Carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas (homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
ABC fire extinguisher, 5 to 10 lb, mounted in a visible, convenient location (still on the April 2026 township checklist)

authorities.name: Not confirmed. Likely Pemberton Township Code Enforcement Division, which checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher during the Certificate of Occupancy Transfer inspection
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application was found. The township CO Transfer checklist covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher. Call Code Enforcement at 609-894-3376 to confirm whether the CO Transfer also serves as the state smoke/CO certificate.

evidence.quote: LEAID: 0329-999 Enf Auth. State Fire Official Louis Kilmer Phone (609)633-6132
A smoke detector is required on each level of the premises. On levels where bedrooms exist, detectors must be located in all bedrooms and outside of each sleeping area.
An ABC fire extinguisher must be no smaller than 5lbs., no larger than 10lbs., and mounted in a visible convenient location.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is the fire code enforcing agency for Pemberton Township (LEA registry code S; state directory lists Fire Official Louis Kilmer, (609)633-6132, LEA name "Pemberton Twp Fire Prev"). The DCA state-towns list (revised 7/17/2026) lists Pemberton Twp without the "SC" (smoke certs) flag, so the state does not appear to issue smoke certificates here, and the directory's Smoke Detector Compliance block is blank. No official page names who issues the certificate; the township CO Transfer inspection checks the same items.

other_items.label: Tax, water, sewer and solid waste accounts paid; liens checked
other_items.detail: The Resale Application has Tax Office and Public Works sign-off lines: liens checked, taxes paid, solid waste, water and sewer accounts paid, and sewer/water units billed.

other_items.label: Well and septic reports
other_items.detail: The Housing Office intake checklist asks for a well report and septic report to be attached (for properties on well or septic).

other_items.label: Open permits, code violations and vacant property fees
other_items.detail: Housing Office checks open construction permits, open code violations and vacant property registration fees before issuing.

other_items.label: Buyer assuming the certificate
other_items.detail: If the buyer takes responsibility for obtaining the certificate, the office must be told in writing before it is issued.

open_questions: Who issues the state smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate in Pemberton Township? The state is the LEA but does not list Pemberton Twp for smoke certs; confirm with Code Enforcement (609-894-3376) whether the CO Transfer covers it.
Is there a rush or late fee, or a minimum lead time before closing? None is published.
How long is the issued certificate valid? Only the 60-day application expiry is stated.
Confirm whether the extinguisher is still required given P.L.2025, c.19; the April 2026 checklist still lists it.
